correctness.rationale: The exact column triple predicate is equivalent to induced maximum degree<=1. Sixteen-state trace maps bijectively to cyclic legal words; integer Newton identities prove the displayed degree-six determinant. The successor-empty injection proves dissociation number <=n and exhaustively classifies equality; four-state cyclic binary automaton has characteristic (lambda^2-lambda-1)(lambda^2+lambda+1), producing Lucas and cubic-root terms. The standalone checker independently matches 1,398,080 subsets at n=3..10 and all extremal counts n=3..40. Formal proof covers all n>=3.

originality.rationale: Published primary literature located treats 3-path-cover algorithms, open grid all-set counts, cyclic-grid inclusion-maximal counts, or general cubic bounds. None of the materially inspected results asserts the all-set cycle-prism polynomial and exact Lucas maximum multiplicity. Comparison is at the level of object, boundary condition, quantifier and selected-set predicate, not title similarity. The cyclic-grid maximal paper was not fully accessible and is flagged as a priority risk.
residual_risks: Only abstract/metadata could be inspected for Tian and Tu (2024): a cyclical-grid specialization is plausible, although its explicit subject is inclusion-maximal sets rather than all sets.
A differently indexed cyclic two-row transfer formula could be published under cylindrical-grid or 1-dependent-set terminology without identical keywords.
No independent mathematical review has been performed; finite enumeration stops at order ten.

value.rationale: The exact all-size enumerator of a canonical connected cubic family and structural classification of maximum dissociation sets answer a natural enumeration question left by scalar and open-grid work. Its exact Lucas law, modulo-three correction, and even-order double-empty exception give a nontrivial count of optimum solutions, equivalently of minimum 3-path vertex covers. This is not a mere table lookup, arbitrary finite slice, or restatement of the size optimum.
